simple_description: The most common type of headache, feeling like a constant dull ache or tight band pressing around both sides of the head, usually caused by stress, posture, or muscle tension.
medical_description: A primary headache disorder characterized by bilateral, pressing or tightening (non-pulsating) pain of mild to moderate intensity. It is not aggravated by routine physical activity, and lacks nausea, with at most one of photophobia or phonophobia present.
affected_system: Pericranial myofascial tissues, peripheral nociceptive afferents, and central pain processing mechanisms.
symptoms: Dull, aching, non-throbbing pain across forehead, temples, or back of head
Sensation of a tight rubber band or vice gripping the skull
Bilateral distribution (both sides of the head)
Tenderness in neck, shoulder, and scalp muscles upon palpation
Mild to moderate intensity that does not prevent daily tasks
early_warning_signs: Gradual tightening in the neck and shoulders after prolonged desk work or stress
possible_causes: Sensitization of central nociceptive neurons in chronic forms
Sustained muscle contraction, poor posture, and emotional strain
risk_factors: Mental or emotional stress and anxiety
Prolonged computer or mobile screen use with poor ergonomic posture
disease_types: Chronic tension-type headache (>= 15 days/month for > 3 months)
clinical_evaluation: Clinical diagnosis based on ICHD-3 criteria. Neurological examination is completely normal aside from pericranial muscle tenderness on manual palpation.
diagnostic_tests: Neuroimaging (CT/MRI) is typically NOT indicated unless red flags or abnormal neurological signs exist
treatment_overview: Simple analgesics (Paracetamol, Ibuprofen, Naproxen) for episodic attacks. For chronic tension headache, low-dose Amitriptyline is the primary evidence-based prophylaxis, combined with physical therapy and stress management.
medication_classes: Chronic prophylaxis: Tricyclic antidepressants (Amitriptyline 10-50 mg nocte), Mirtazapine
precautions: Avoid taking simple analgesics on more than 14 days per month to prevent Medication-Overuse Headache
Do not use opioids or combination sedatives
prevention: Maintain ergonomic desk setup with monitor at eye level
Practice progressive relaxation exercises and neck stretches
Ensure regular 7-8 hours sleep and adequate hydration
complications: Chronification leading to chronic tension-type headache and analgesic overuse
emergency_signs: Headache that is sudden and explosive (thunderclap)
Associated with new neurological deficits, stiff neck, or fever

faqs.question: How can I tell Tension headache from Migraine?
faqs.answer: Tension headache feels like a tight dull band on *both* sides of the head and is not worsened by walking. Migraine is usually on *one* side, throbs with your heartbeat, and causes nausea or extreme light sensitivity.

hi.name: टेंशन सिरदर्द (Tension-type headache)
hi.summary: सिर के दोनों तरफ पट्टी बंधे होने जैसा भारी दबाव और धीमा दर्द जो तनाव, गर्दन में खिंचाव या नींद की कमी से होता है।
hi.advice: गर्दन की स्ट्रेचिंग करें, स्क्रीन से ब्रेक लें, पानी पिएं और तनाव कम करने के उपाय अपनाएं।

hinglish.name: Tension Headache (Sar me tight patti bandha jaisa dard)
hinglish.summary: Dono taraf bhari dabav mehsoos hona, ulti nahi aati, stress ya computer screen se badhta hai.
hinglish.advice: Rest karein, posture theek karein aur paracetamol le sakte hain.
